newsitem.title: UK: Copper drives lower by LME close, longs liquidate.
newsitem.headline: Copper drives lower by LME close, longs liquidate.

text.p: Long liquidation following recent Chinese sales and market talk that several shorts were expecting a downturn in copper prices prompted a selling spree during active London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Tuesday.
The waves of selling negated falling LME warehouse stocks, with the market ignoring a 13,475-tonne fall on Tuesday which left total inventories at a six-year low of 132,350 tonnes.
Several traders suggested that long positions once belonging to Japan's Sumitomo Corp were still being sold into rallies, although others remain unconvinced.
Three months delivery copper was last at $1,925, down from Monday's $2,016 close after ranging between $2,102 and $1,916 throughout the session.
"The recent rise in copper prices had become overdone and we are seeing a knee-jerk reaction at the nervous end of the market," one LME floor trader said.

Supporting the unwinding of Sumitomo positions a senior floor trader said, "It may be possible that this is the final stage of the Sumitomo long...After all it had to be liquidated fully to settle the market."

But most LME floor traders agreed that Tuesday's gyrations in the market were a welcome relief after recent hand-cuffed trading movements. Support for copper is now seen at $1,900 in late London trading.
"Its like a breath of fresh air - we have seen a major move compared with recent tight and low volume movements," one trader said.
Other metals, although ending lower, failed to match the declines in the copper market.
"There has been no widespread liquidation as we await the next move in copper," a trader said.
Consumer buying helped underpin aluminium, aiding a recovery from an earlier dip below $1,400. It was last at $1,408, versus $1,415.50.
Zinc after recent investment fund buying slipped with copper to $1,042, a loss of $12. Lead was down $9 at $737, although trade interest ahead of the European U.S. winter was evident.
Tin was also under pressure but held key support near $5,900. It was last at $5,930, down $70.
Nickel in tandam with copper lost all of its recent gains and tumbled to $7,340, against $7,409. On Monday prices hit a high of $7,450. Alloy was last at $1,280, versus $1,266.
